text: I'm Daniel Park, CTO of TensorGate. Here's the technical problem.
A bank wants to use a large language model on customer data,
but the moment that data leaves their environment, compliance says no.
So what we built is a gateway that runs inside a hardware enclave.
The prompt is decrypted only inside the enclave.
And we generate a cryptographic attestation for every single request
so the security team can prove exactly what code...
touched the data. The hard part, honestly, was latency. Enclaves used to add seconds. We got
the overhead down to about 40 milliseconds by batching attestation and pinning memory. Four
design partners in banking and healthcare, two already on paid contracts, 31 million requests
served. We're raising a $4 million seed. The insight's simple. If you can prove where the
data went, regulated companies can finally say yes.
